rules.problem: Trigger 'Pain of skin' matches the page title but is not a recorded common symptom or warning sign, so the task may rarely fire. The red box only cross-refers to p82 ('Check if the patient needs urgent attention 82'), so having no priority evaluation here is right. The check list covers every discriminator on the page.

The and-structure matches 'Red, warm, painful lump', and the optional 'may be fluctuant / may discharge pus' is correctly left out. But the evidence is generic Erythema + Warm skin + Pain of skin + Mass of skin, so nothing excludes a cellulitis/erysipelas patient who also has a skin mass. The diagnosis concept also misses 'boil' (Furuncle is not a descendant).
Faithful to 'Red, warm, swollen skin' → poorly-defined borders → Cellulitis likely. The only issue is the generic Erythema base concept.
Faithful to 'Red, warm, swollen skin' → clearly-defined raised borders → Erysipelas likely. The only issue is the generic Erythema base concept.

'If recurrent boils or abscesses: if painful abscesses in axilla, groin or perineum, hidradenitis suppurativa likely' maps well to an or-list of Recurrent abscess of skin with finding sites. Pain is required, matching 'painful abscesses'.

summary: Nothing invented or misplaced. All five 'likely' diagnoses are probable rules with and/or structure that follows the page, and the red box is only a cross-reference to p82, so having no priority rule is correct. The most consequential issue is the boil/abscess rule: its diagnosis concept does not cover 'boil' (Furuncle is not a descendant), and its generic evidence (Erythema, Warm skin, Pain of skin, Mass of skin) overlaps the cellulitis presentation. Second, every red-skin condition uses the generic 'Erythema' where (snomed_concept "Erythema of skin" "disorder") exists. Out of scope for the claims but worth noting: 'Suspected meningitis' appears only as a herpes zoster referral criterion and is not encoded as a possible diagnosis.
